claim: Consider the preferred-orientation Kagome quantum graph of Baradaran and Exner with positive edge lengths \(b=d-c\) and \(c\) satisfying \(b/c\notin\mathbb Q\). For the high-energy universal spectral-probability constant determined by their asymptotic band criterion (3.13), set \(q_0=\sqrt{3/5}\), \(a(q)=2q-\sqrt{4q^2+3}\), \(b_+(q)=2q+\sqrt{4q^2+3}\), \(g(q)=3/q\), and \(e(q)=-(3+q^2)/(2q)\) for \(q>0\). Define \(h_<(q)=1+\pi^{-1}(\arctan e(q)+\arctan b_+(q)-\arctan a(q)-\arctan g(q))\) and \(h_>(q)=1+\pi^{-1}(\arctan e(q)+\arctan g(q)-\arctan a(q)-\arctan b_+(q))\). Then the universal constant has the exact one-dimensional representation \[P_\mathrm{Kag}=\frac{2}{\pi}\left(\int_0^{q_0}\frac{h_<(q)}{1+q^2}\,dq+\int_{q_0}^{\infty}\frac{h_>(q)}{1+q^2}\,dq\right)=0.639080422792129545\ldots.\] The reduction follows from the tangent half-angle factorization of the source's two-phase criterion: with \(p=\tan(x/2)\) and \(q=\tan(y/2)\), its sign is the sign of \((3-p^2+4pq)(3-pq)(3+q^2+2pq)\); the only positive-root ordering change occurs at \(q=q_0\).

correctness.rationale: The published two-phase criterion is transformed by p=tan(x/2), q=tan(y/2) into a polynomial sign condition with only a nonnegative omitted multiplier. For fixed q>0 the four roots are explicit; their ordering is proved, the sole crossover solves q^2=3/5, and integrating the standard-Cauchy conditional intervals gives the stated one-dimensional formula. The q<0 half follows from F(-p,-q)=F(p,q). The change from momentum to energy weighting preserves the limiting fraction by integration by parts. The standalone checker reproduces the integral and independently checks the original torus area numerically.

value.rationale: The spectral probability is a principal transport statistic of the motivating paper. The source's incommensurate value was obtained from a two-dimensional numerical area after stating that the inequality was analytically unwieldy. The new factorization reduces the region exactly to one-dimensional Cauchy quadrature, exposes a single algebraic transition at sqrt(3/5), improves reproducibility and precision, and creates a tractable starting point for rigorous bounds or further symbolic analysis.
